final_recommendation: The room converged on inevitable litigation despite FINMA's concessions. Bondholder counsel committed to Monday filing on the ordinance's procedural invalidity, weaponizing FINMA's €2.8B indemnity as evidence of known liability risk. FINMA secured ECB/PRA co-signature banning future emergency ordinance rewrites of viability triggers, but failed to prevent the legal challenge or fully restore AT1 market confidence due to unresolved guidance-workaround concerns and reinsurer-funded defense tail.
minority_objections: FINMA legal argued the Article 36(1) ordinance was procedurally sound and that indemnity reflected prudent governance, not admission of invalidity
Credit market analyst warned that litigation itself wouldn't restore AT1 pricing unless FINMA closed the regulatory-guidance loophole for viability redefinition
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel vs FINMA legal on whether indemnity language constituted admission of ordinance invalidity (counsel weaponized it; FINMA denied)
AT1 bondholder group vs FINMA on recovery framework timing and scope (group demanded 50% asset carve-out; FINMA refused as exceeding authority)
Institutional investor vs FINMA on whether Thursday statement closed guidance-workaround for future viability redefinition (investor demanded explicit ban; FINMA initially resisted)
key_concessions: FINMA committed €2.8B indemnity covering defense costs and viability judgment exposure across US/UK/Swiss jurisdictions by Monday
FINMA secured ECB/PRA co-signature by Thursday explicitly banning future emergency ordinance rewrites of viability triggers
FINMA funded independent claims reviewer and committed to 90-day mediation timeline with binding confidentiality
Bondholder counsel agreed to separate administrative claim for asset recovery rather than tying it to ordinance litigation
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: no pause on Monday filing unless FINMA admits ordinance created director liability exposure in writing
FINMA legal: will not concede ordinance was unlawful or commit to retroactive AT1 hierarchy restoration
AT1 bondholder group: no re-entry to AT1 market without binding recovery terms and equity-subordination guarantee this week
Reinsurers (via insurance observer): will fund litigation independently if indemnity scope leaves gaps in three-jurisdiction coverage
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The regulatory-guidance workaround for viability redefinition remained unresolved until R8, allowing dealers to continue repricing all bank AT1 as subordinated
The 4-6 year reinsurer-funded defense tail was acknowledged but not structurally addressed beyond the indemnity cap
Cross-border coordination risk (ECB/PRA co-signature delivery) was assumed rather than stress-tested
The precedent effect on non-Swiss banks' AT1 issuance was discussed but not quantified or mitigated
downstream_risk_variables: Reinsurer commitment to independent funding if indemnity gaps emerge post-Monday filing
ECB/PRA willingness to co-sign Thursday statement banning ordinance rewrites and guidance workarounds
Rating agency and primary dealer response to Thursday statement's scope (ordinance-only vs mechanism-agnostic)
Duration and outcome of 90-day mediation on asset recovery framework
Court rulings on ordinance procedural validity across US/UK/Swiss jurisdictions over 12-18 months
uncertainty_notes: The room failed to resolve whether Thursday's statement would explicitly ban viability redefinition via regulatory guidance (not just emergency ordinance), leaving dealers uncertain about future AT1 subordination risk. Reinsurer defense-funding commitment remained contingent on final indemnity language. The 4-6 year claims tail was capped financially but not structurally shortened. Cross-border regulatory alignment (ECB/PRA co-signature) was assumed but not confirmed by meeting end.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Bondholder counsel formally committed to Monday filing in R6, weaponizing FINMA's indemnity as evidence; litigation became inevitable despite FINMA concessions and drove every subsequent negotiation
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Counsel's constitutional attack on the 19 March ordinance (procedural invalidity, emergency law rewrite) was the central legal strategy from R1 onward; FINMA's defense of Article 36(1) emergency powers shaped all concessions
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Equity-AT1 inversion (equity got UBS shares, AT1 wiped to zero) was the foundational grievance driving litigation threat, recovery demands, and market repricing concerns throughout
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 repricing and future issuance concerns were consistently raised (R2-R8) but remained secondary to litigation strategy and hierarchy precedent; became more prominent in R7-R8 re guidance-workaround
marker_evidence.claims_tail: The 3-5 year (later 4-6 year) D&O/E&O reinsurer-funded defense tail was a recurring, structurally developed theme from R3 onward, shaping indemnity scope negotiations and settlement math
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O carrier and reinsurer exposure was explicitly discussed from R1 and shaped indemnity negotiations (R3-R8), but remained instrumental to claims-tail analysis rather than a standalone driver
